text:
maria: We need a new GPU node pool in ap-se2 for latency-sensitive inference. Targets: ~12 reserved GPUs for steady traffic, burstable capacity up to ~80 GPUs for spikes, static egress IPs for model downloads, and strict PDBs for critical pods. Thoughts on instance mix + autoscaler config?

raj: Quota check: ap-se2 shows only ~12 GPUs free right now. Provider quota increases are ~3-5 days. If we need capacity before the request is fully approved, plan to create a small reserved pool + larger preemptible burst pool.

kevin: Agreed. Also we must ensure GPU nodes use a NAT with reserved static IPs so downloads don't come from ephemeral addresses and break customer allowlists. We should tag routes so only gpu pools egress via NAT.

 taylor: Proposed layout: 
- reserved-pool: 6 x A100 (steady, taint gpu=reserved:NoSchedule), keep small AZ spread
- reserve-bump: 6 x A100 (can scale to 12 when quota approved)
- burst-pool: 0..80 x A10G (preemptible/spot, taint gpu=burst:NoSchedule)
Use PriorityClass + Pod tolerations to pin critical inference to reserved nodes.

maria: Autoscaler notes: prefer cluster-autoscaler with multiple node groups, set autoscaler expander to least-waste and enable --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false? We should also tune balance-similar-node-groups=false so CA doesn't try to rebalance across hetero pools.

raj: For cooldowns, use conservative scaleDownDelay for reserved pool (30m) and aggressive scaleDown for burst (5m). Also set maxNodesProvisionedPerCycle low to avoid overshoot during sudden traffic bursts.

kevin: NAT plan: I'll provision one or two static NAT IPs, attach to a NAT gateway in the VPC, and create a route-tagging rule so only nodes labeled pool=gpu use that NAT. Will also update firewall/outbound rules.

maria: Example commands (adjust for provider):

```
# burst pool (preemptible)
cloudctl node-pools create gpu-burst \n  --cluster redwood-apse2 \n  --machine-type n2-standard-32 \n  --min-nodes 0 --max-nodes 80 --initial-node-count 0 \n  --accelerator type=nvidia-a10g,count=1 \n  --node-taints gpu=burst:NoSchedule \n  --node-labels pool=burst,gpu=type-a10g
```

```
# reserved pool (steady)
cloudctl node-pools create gpu-reserved \n  --cluster redwood-apse2 \n  --machine-type n2-highmem-64 \n  --num-nodes 6 \n  --accelerator type=nvidia-a100,count=1 \n  --node-taints gpu=reserved:NoSchedule \n  --node-labels pool=reserved,gpu=type-a100
```

maria: Kubernetes manifest notes:
- PriorityClass: critical-infer (value high)
- PodDisruptionBudget: minAvailable=2 for critical replicas
- PodTopologySpread across zones to avoid AZ clumping
- tolerations for reserved/burst taints and nodeSelector by pool label

taylor: I'll prepare a PR with example PriorityClass, tolerations, PDB, and a sample PodTopologySpread. Will also add sample HPA vs external traffic scaler guidance.

raj: Quota action: opening ticket Q-4412 to request +80 GPUs (mix A100 and A10G SKUs) for ap-se2. Include urgency and test plan.

infra-bot: quota-scan result: region=ap-se2 total_quota=200 used=188 free=12. Recommendation: open quota increment Q-4412. Provider ETA: 72-96h.

kevin: I'll try to get NAT/EIP and route tagging done by EOD tomorrow and post the reserved IPs for allowlist updates.

maria: Action items:
- raj: file quota ticket Q-4412 and request +80 GPUs (A100+A10G)
- kevin: provision NAT with reserved EIPs and route tagging for gpu pools
- taylor: PR with k8s manifests (PriorityClass, tolerations, PDB, TopologySpread)
- infra: create burst pool (0..80) now, keep reserved pool at 6 until quota approved

kevin: Will post IPs here when ready.

maria: Once quota is approved we'll scale reserved pool to 12, run a 2-replica canary on reserved nodes, then enable burst scaling for load tests. Ping me when NAT IPs are live. :thumbsup:
